atmosphere.value: toluene as process control reagent (to avoid oxidation)

processing_steps_notes.value: Parent process (proc_ma-35h). Starting elemental powder Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si and C (99.2% pure) in Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 proportion; planetary ball mill Retsch PM 400/2 at 200 rpm, ball-to-powder ratio 10:1, tungsten carbide (WC) vials and WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating. This 35 h milled powder is the starting material for the 500 °C anneal.

source.reason: This is the defining processing step of the sample (500 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching), reported in the experimental section and the thermal-stability study.

processing_steps_notes.value: 35 h milled powder was annealed for 1 h at 500 °C (one of 400, 500, 600 and 800 °C conditions) followed by water quenching, to study thermal stability. ~500 °C is the upper bound of thermal stability of the milled powder.

source.reason: The overall multiphase structure of the 500 °C annealed powder is described in the thermal-stability results/discussion and quantified in Table 4 (500 °C row).

overall_structure.value: Multiphase structure retained at 500 °C: BCC (major phase) + γ-brass type + partially ordered B2-type, with a trace amount of undissolved Si. The metastable milled alloy remains thermally stable at 500 °C; no Fe5Si3-type silicide is formed (it appears only from 600 °C onward).

instrument_or_setup.value: Netzsch DSC404 Pegasus differential scanning calorimeter

measurement_conditions.value: 35 h milled powder heated up to 1000 °C at 20 K/min under nitrogen (N2) atmosphere

purpose.value: Study the thermal stability of the milled powder and locate exothermic events that guided the annealing temperatures

key_findings.value: Exothermic events at ~420 °C (693 K) attributed to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase and at ~520 °C (793 K) attributed to Fe5Si3-type silicide formation; the 500 °C annealing condition lies below the 520 °C silicide event.

source.reason: The CALPHAD (Thermo-Calc, TCFE8) single-point equilibrium calculation includes the 500 °C/773 K condition, the annealing temperature of this sample, and was used to correlate the phases formed during annealing.

simulation_method.value: CALPHAD thermodynamic modelling (property diagram and single-point equilibrium calculation)

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Pressure = 100000.0 Pa; system size = 1.0 mol; mole fraction Mn = 0.19, Ni = 0.15, Al = 0.15, Si = 0.10, C = 0.01 (balance Fe). Single-point equilibrium at 1200, 1100, 800, 500 and 300 °C — at 500 °C (773 K) predicted phases: BCC_A2#1 = 0.69, B2 = 0.28, BCC_A2#2 = 0.02, M3Si = 0.01 mol.

validation_against_experiment.value: CALPHAD-predicted phases (BCC, partially ordered B2, γ-brass type) were correlated with the experimentally observed phases of the annealed/SPSed samples; differences between prediction and experiment are attributed to use of the TCFE8 database instead of TCHEA3.

unmapped_findings: The 35 h milled powder is thermally stable up to ~500 °C; at the 500 °C annealing condition the phases BCC + γ-brass type + B2-type are retained and no Fe5Si3-type silicide is formed (the silicide appears only from 600 °C onward).

DTA of the 35 h milled powder shows two exothermic events, at ~420 °C (693 K) assigned to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase and at ~520 °C (793 K) assigned to the formation of the Fe5Si3-type phase; the 500 °C annealing temperature is below the 520 °C silicide-formation event.
Rietveld refinement quality for the 500 °C annealed sample: wR = 2.279, GoF = 1.04, χ² = 1.07.

Room-temperature phase assemblage of the milled/annealed alloy is reported as BCC + γ-brass type + B2 + Si (undissolved). At 500 °C the γ-brass type phase fraction increased relative to the as-milled powder, and some new peaks evolved (Fig. 5 deconvolution around the BCC (110) peak).

No mechanical/physical property measurements (microhardness, elastic modulus, compressive strength, density) were performed on the 500 °C annealed powder; the reported values 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa microhardness, 184 ± 5 GPa elastic modulus and 2046 ± 160 MPa compressive strength with ~19% ductility belong to the SPSed sample, not to this annealed-powder sample.
